subject: arts-music
essential_question: How can understanding studio techniques and design problems help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Apply three-dimensional design independently in a new representation, text, situation, or design constraint.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of three-dimensional design.
Check, revise, or improve work about three-dimensional design using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about three-dimensional design.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
task_brief: Day 4 of "Studio Techniques and Design Problems" (unit 2, grade 7) is an independent application on three-dimensional design. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Solve a design challenge through sketches, prototypes, final work, and critique. Today's work contributes to that by handling three-dimensional design at the independent application a stage, against the unit's wider topics of drawing and observation, painting or color media, print collage or mixed media, and three-dimensional design. This session produces reviewable evidence toward the unit performance task.
primary_task: Independently make one short original piece built around three-dimensional design, aiming at an effect you choose in advance. Write the intended effect first, in one sentence, before you begin. Make the piece, then step back and judge honestly whether the effect landed, citing the specific element that carries it and one element that works against it. Revise that second element and keep both versions. The work must be your own; a tutor may demonstrate technique or give feedback but must not make any part of the graded piece. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about three-dimensional design, and it belongs to "Studio Techniques and Design Problems", which also covers separate topics such as drawing and observation. Close out with this check before you stop: In one concise response, show or explain the most important idea about three-dimensional design; then identify one check that would catch an error or weak claim. At grade 7 the bar is independent work with reasoning that a reader can follow without you present, plus one stated check you ran on your own result before submitting.
requirements: Meet this lesson's own success criteria: The learner completes the central task about three-dimensional design., The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
Address the lesson objective: Apply three-dimensional design independently in a new representation, text, situation, or design constraint.
Produce the deliverable for an independent application: One original short piece, a pre-written intent statement, a two-element self-critique, and a revision with both versions kept.
Show the process, not only the result — a working log, draft, or annotated study.
Complete the critique criteria list in this package before submitting.
deliverable: One original short piece, a pre-written intent statement, a two-element self-critique, and a revision with both versions kept.
critique_criteria: The intended effect was written in one sentence before work began.
The finished piece is original and uses the lesson's focus to pursue that effect.
The self-critique cites one element that carries the intent and one that works against it.
A revision of the weaker element exists and both versions are kept.
The graded piece is the student's own authorship; assistance did not make any part of it.

presentation_and_privacy.presentation_options: You choose the audience. Keeping the work entirely to yourself, showing it to one parent or trusted adult, or submitting it as a file with no one watching are all full-credit options. No public performance, exhibition, class presentation, live audience, photograph, camera, or voice recording is required at any point in this task, and choosing the most private option never lowers the score.
presentation_and_privacy.text_or_no_audio_alternative: A written alternative is always available and scores the same. Instead of performing, speaking, or recording, you may submit a written description of what you made or would make, a notated or diagrammed version, a labelled plan, or a written analysis covering the same criteria. Nothing in this task requires a working microphone, camera, or the ability to perform aloud.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any material you did not create yourself must be in the public domain, openly licensed, or used as a short cited excerpt for study — reproduce no more than the point requires, credit the maker and the source, and never copy full lyrics, a complete score, or a whole image and present it as your own.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: This work spans sessions, so supply a written milestone plan, explicit checkpoint dates, and a task breakdown. Executive-function load — sequencing, holding the plan in mind, remembering where the work stopped — must not become a silent part of what is being assessed.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Protect hearing, ventilation, tool safety, copyright, cultural context, and respectful representation.
Provide a non-performance or low-audience option when needed without lowering the academic target.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting three-dimensional design.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for three-dimensional design follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for three-dimensional design, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for three-dimensional design works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of three-dimensional design, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking three-dimensional design mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply three-dimensional design under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on three-dimensional design rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays private by default and uses only original, public-domain, or properly cited material. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
